state_background_check.value: Florida has a facially broad state constitutional disqualification, but it cannot reach a candidate for the U.S. House or Senate. Fla. Const. Art. VI, §4(a) bars anyone 'convicted of a felony' from being 'qualified to vote or hold office until restoration of civil rights or removal of disability' — text not expressly limited to state office. However, under the Qualifications Clauses (U.S. Const. Art. I, §2, cl.2 for the House; §3, cl.3 for the Senate) as construed in U.S. Term Limits, Inc. v. Thornton, 514 U.S. 779 (1995), states may not add qualifications for Congress beyond the Constitution's own age/citizenship/residency requirements, and each chamber alone judges its members' qualifications (Art. I, §5). Confirming this in practice: Florida's own 2024 Federal Qualifying Handbook (FL Division of Elections) lists only the three federal constitutional qualifications for U.S. House and Senate candidates (citizenship years, age, state inhabitancy) — no felony or background-check requirement appears anywhere in the federal candidate-qualifying chapters — and Fla. Stat. §99.012 ('Restrictions on individuals qualifying for public office') likewise contains no criminal-history provision and expressly exempts 'persons holding any federal office' from its concurrent-term resign-to-run rule. No FL statute or rule requires a background check as part of federal candidate qualifying.
state_background_check.snippet: No person convicted of a felony, or adjudicated in this or any other state to be mentally incompetent, shall be qualified to vote or hold office until restoration of civil rights or removal of disability.

employment_record.snippet: Scott served our nation as a Naval Aviator for 26 years, (14 active and 12 reserve) flying combat missions and operating from the decks of 13 aircraft carriers. He deployed to the Mediterranean, the Persian Gulf, and the North Atlantic, with combat operations in the Gulf, Bosnia, and Kosovo. After the attacks of September 11, he was recalled to active duty with U.S. Central Command. His military experience instilled in him the importance of strength, accountability, and putting America first. After his military service, Scott ran a successful insurance business in Lakeland, Florida for two decades.

bio_summary.value: A native of Brooklyn, NY, Deva relocated to Florida in 1995 and has proudly called Polk County home since 2002. With over 20 years in education, she has dedicated her life to empowering students and families through learning, mentorship, and community engagement. Her commitment to service extends far beyond the classroom. Deva has served on the Board of the Boys & Girls Club of Lakeland, is a proud sponsor of the AGB Museum of Art, and volunteers with kidsPACK, Alpha Kappa Alpha Sorority, Incorporated®, and Polk County Schools. Now, Deva is stepping up to serve on a greater level — as a candidate for U.S. Congress, District 18.
